data.description:
Spend Friday afternoons and Sunday mornings at Rock Creek Park learning about our wild and wonderful urban oasis!  Park Rangers will teach kids (and people of all ages) about the fantastic flora and fauna in the park.

data.title: Fun with Flora and Fauna

data.location: Peirce Mill is located at 2401 Tilden St NW.
data.description: Step inside Peirce Mill, a rare surviving 19th-century gristmill in Rock Creek Park, and discover how waterpower once supported daily life in Washington, DC. Built in the 1820s, the mill served local farmers by grinding grain into flour and cornmeal. On this guided tour, you’ll explore the mill’s machinery, including the waterwheel, gears, and millstones that brought the process to life. Learn how the force of Rock Creek was harnessed to power the mill and the skill required to operate it. Rangers will share stories of the Peirce family and the workers who kept the mill running.
data.title: Ranger Tours at Peirce Mill

data.location: Meet outside the Old Stone House at 3051 M St NW, Washington, D.C. 20007.
data.description:
Join a ranger on a walk to learn about Georgetown during one of the most turbulent chapters in American history. From the divided loyalties of Georgetown residents to the presence of Union soldiers, this tour reveals the hidden stories of a community caught between North and South. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring water. This hike will utilize sidewalks that can be narrow and uneven at times. It will traverse nearly two miles of neighborhood streets in the Georgetown area of DC.  

Tour departs from the Old Stone House.

There are no public facilities available on this hike. 

Recommended for ages 12 and up.

Walk may be cancelled in the event of bad weather at the discretion of park staff. Feel free to check the Rock Creek Park website the day of to confirm. Or call the Nature Center (202-895-6070) the day of to confirm and be sure to leave a voicemail for a callback.
data.title: The Civil War in Georgetown: A Guided Walk in a City Divided

data.location: The Old Stone House is located on 3051 M Street NW
data.description: Step back in time with a ranger-led tour of the Old Stone House, the oldest building in the nation’s capital. Discover what life was like in the 18th century as you explore its simple rooms, learn about early residents, and uncover the stories hidden within its stone walls. Perfect for visitors of all ages, this short tour offers a glimpse into everyday colonial life right in the heart of the city.

data.description:
Join a ranger for a 30-minute, family-friendly walk through Battleground National Cemetery and discover the stories of the soldiers buried here. Learn who these men were and how their service helped shape our nation's history.  

Uncover clues about the lives of the soldiers, and think about how we remember people who served long ago. Through stories, questions, and observation, children and families will gain a deeper appreciation for the sacrifices made during one of the most important chapters in American history.  

Perfect for families with children ages 6 and up. This easy walking tour lasts approximately 30 minutes.
data.title: Heroes Remembered: Stories from Battleground National Cemetery

data.description:
Calling all future Junior Rangers! Get ready to travel back in time, uncover amazing stories, and discover what life was really like during the Civil War! At the Junior Ranger Discovery Club, every meeting is a new adventure. Collect Civil War trading cards, investigate what soldiers and families ate, discover what Civil War uniforms and equipment can tell us about the people who wore them, and try fun, hands-on activities that bring history to life. 
 
Complete challenges, ask questions, make discoveries, and learn how Junior Rangers can help protect the historic places and stories found in our national parks. 
 
Explore the past. Learn something new. Protect our parks. And have fun doing it! 
Recommended Ages: 8–12
data.title: Junior Ranger Discovery Club: Explore, Learn, Protect

During this ½ mile excursion, beginner explorers learn the hiking essentials, such as trail safety, what to wear or bring to a hike, and how to Recreate Responsibly all while looking at and respecting nature found in our woodlands.  This ranger-led hike is intended to create treasured trail experiences for families interested in planning more advance hikes as their children become more experienced.  

Additional Information:   This hike is recommended for families with children ages 5 and up. Meet at the Rock Creek Park Nature Center porch, bring plenty of water, dress for the weather, and be prepared for a fun and enjoyable outing.

data.description:
Join a National Park Service ranger for a guided walk-through Battleground National Cemetery to explore Civil War monuments, their symbols, and the stories they were built to preserve. Discover how art, memory, and history come together in this quiet landscape where Washington, DC’s past is written in stone. As a part of the Freedom 250 commemoration, this program invites visitors to reflect on sacrifice, citizenship, and the enduring power of public memory.   
 
Please note that parking is limited to public streets.
data.title: Stories in Stone: Monuments at Battleground National Cemetery

data.location: The Nature Center and Planetarium is located at 5200 Glover Rd NW Washington, D.C. 20015. Meet the ranger on the front porch.
data.description:
The Milkhouse Ford trail offers both beautifully forested nature and a glimpse into Washington DC’s history. Ramble with a ranger for a guided hike on this 1.7-mile loop, where you will encounter 5000 years of history, from traces of Indigenous land usage, to Fort DeRussy (which saw action during the Civil War), to the two-room log cabin used by poet Joaquin Miller, and to the historic Milkhouse Ford river crossing (one of Rock Creek Park’s oldest and most well-preserved fords).  Meet at the Rock Creek Park Nature Center, bring plenty of water, dress for the weather, and be prepared for a fun and enjoyable outing.  

For this Halloween hike, wear your costume!
data.title: Echoes of Time in Rock Creek Park Guided Hike

data.description:
Calling all dog owners! If you enjoy adventuring in Rock Creek Park with your furry friend, consider coming to one of our B.A.R.K. Ranger events! This is a national initiative to encourage responsible recreation and a positive experience for you, your dog, and all visitors to the park.    

Learn about the principles of being a B.A.R.K. Ranger and earn a B.A.R.K. Ranger badge! A ranger will be present to induct the new B.A.R.K. Rangers and distribute some fun doggie giveaways! A photo op will also be available to commemorate this great achievement!    

So how does one become a B.A.R.K. Ranger? By pledging to:   

Bag your pet’s waste   

Always leash your pet   

Respect wildlife   

Know where you can go   

We hope you can bring your canine pals and join the fun!  We encourage you to bring your pup in a Halloween costume!

images.altText: a black dog on a leash wears a brown ranger hat prop and a colorful bandana
images.caption: Swear your dog in as a B.A.R.K. Ranger and they may get a chance to wear this cool hat.

data.location: Peirce Mill is located at 2401 Tilden St NW Washington, D.C. 20008
data.description:
Lace up your hiking boots and follow in the footsteps of Theodore Roosevelt, the adventurous president who believed that time spent in nature built character, courage, and a stronger nation. Beginning at Peirce Mill, this 1.5-mile (round-trip) guided hike winds through scenic trails and rugged landscapes that Roosevelt explored while escaping the pressures of the presidency.   

This hike covers uneven, tight, rocky terrain with steep elevation changes and may be challenging for some visitors. Participants should wear sturdy footwear, bring water, and dress appropriately for the weather. Recommended for ages 10 and older.  Children must be accompanied by an adult.

images.altText: an outcropping of vertical rocks with trees overlooking a creek
images.caption: Learn why Pulpit Rock was so important to Theodore Roosevelt on this guided hike.

data.title: Roosevelt at Rock Creek Park
